Updated imports in backend/src/run-agent-step.ts and backend/src/tools.ts to reflect new location. Renamed codebuffTools to codebuffToolDefs in backend/src/tools/constants.ts for clarity.

eli5.text: The team reorganized some internal code that defines which tools the AI assistant can use, moving the tool definitions into a dedicated folder and updating where the rest of the system looks for them. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping, you won't notice any difference in how the assistant works today, but it makes the codebase cleaner and easier to maintain going forward.

ai.title: Refactor thinker agent prompt for conciseness
ai.summary: Updated `userInputPrompt` in `backend/src/templates/agents/thinker.ts` to enforce extreme conciseness. Removed prescriptive guidelines and step-by-step planning instructions, replacing them with directives for short sentences (~5 words) and argument-based reasoning over confident solutions. Scope limited to backend agent templates.

eli5.text: Starting July 3, 2025, the backend's built-in planning assistant was quietly reworded to be more terse and debate-oriented. It now favors short, bullet-like arguments over step-by-step blueprints, nudging engineers toward a quick read rather than a long briefing. This only alters how the assistant drafts its internal notes and does not change any visible feature you'd encounter.

ai.title: Add OpenRouter fallback for Claude models
ai.summary: New `promptAnthropicWithFallbacks` in `anthropic-with-fallbacks.ts` retries Claude requests via OpenRouter if the primary Anthropic API fails. `promptAiSdkStream` intercepts Anthropic calls with configured `fallbackProviders` to trigger this chain. `openrouter-api.ts` maps Claude model IDs to OpenRouter equivalents, using fewer retries (2 vs 3) for fallbacks. Agent templates in `base.ts` enable this by passing `fallbackProviders: ['openrouter']` for Claude models.

eli5.text: When Claude fails, Codebuff retries the request via OpenRouter instead of giving you an error. The retry chain uses the same Claude model names mapped to OpenRouter equivalents, with fewer retry attempts for fallbacks than the primary API. You would only notice if the primary Anthropic API call failed; otherwise, your chat works exactly as before.

ai.title: Remove @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock dependency
ai.summary: Dropped `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` from backend dependencies. Likely cleanup of unused or deprecated provider integration. Scope limited to backend package manifest.

eli5.text: The backend dropped support for connecting to Amazon Bedrock's AI models, so those models are no longer available as an option through our system. This only affects the server side and won't be noticeable unless you were specifically trying to use an Amazon Bedrock model. The change is live today.

ai.title: Fix @ menu trigger on paste
ai.summary: CLI @ agent menu now delays display by 30ms and checks `isPasting` flag to prevent accidental triggers during fast input. Paste detection logic updated to use named constants `PASTE_THRESHOLD_MS` (10ms) and `PASTE_MIN_COUNT` (2). Change confined to `npm-app/src/cli.ts` key press handling and `detectPasting` method.

eli5.text: When you paste text that contains an @ symbol into the command line, the assistant menu no longer pops up accidentally. The system now waits a brief moment after each keystroke to determine whether you're typing normally or pasting a block of text; if it detects a paste, it suppresses the menu until the paste completes. This only affects the command-line interface of the npm app, and the change is already live in the code as of today.

ai.title: Backend support multiple live user inputs per user
ai.summary: Internal backend refactor in `live-user-inputs.ts` changes the `live` map from `Record<string, string>` to `Record<string, string[]>`. `startUserInput` now pushes IDs to an array, `endUserInput` filters them, and `checkLiveUserInput` uses `.some()` to validate against any active input. `ai-sdk.ts` updates log metadata to use the new plural `getLiveUserInputIds` function. This enables concurrent Codebuff instances per user without input cancellation conflicts.

eli5.text: A single person can now run multiple Codebuff sessions at the same time without one cancelling the other. Previously, starting a new session would cut short any session already in progress; now the system keeps a running list of active inputs per person, so ending one session removes only itself from that list and leaves the others untouched. This means you can kick off a second task while the first is still working, and both will keep running to completion. The change is live today.

ai.title: Fix undefined error in checkLiveUserInput
ai.summary: Added guard for undefined user input in `checkLiveUserInput`. Prevents crash when accessing `live[userId]` before checking existence. Scope limited to `backend/src/live-user-inputs.ts`. Logic now returns false if `live[userId]` is undefined.

eli5.text: The system no longer crashes when it tries to check something on a user who doesn't have the thing it's looking for yet, like checking someone's shopping cart when they haven't added anything. It now quietly skips that check instead of throwing an error. This affects the live collaboration feature, which lets multiple people work at once, stopping sudden crashes that could interrupt an active session.

ai.title: Fix terminal command canceling
ai.summary: CLI stop handler now cancels current input via Client.cancelCurrentInput. Spinner start calls moved to ensure proper cleanup before stopping. Tool-call response spinners updated to 'Processing results...' and 'Fixing...' states.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C during a response, the program will now actually stop the current input instead of hanging. You'll notice the spinner text changes from 'Thinking...' to 'Processing results...' or 'Fixing...' depending on what's happening. This is already live today in the npm app.

ai.title: Downgrade endUserInput mismatch log to DEBUG
ai.summary: In backend/src/live-user-inputs.ts, the logger call for mismatched endUserInput attempts changed from error to debug. This reduces noise for expected race conditions or stale IDs during user input termination. The payload structure remains identical.

eli5.text: When you finish typing a reply, the app used to log an error if the request didn't match what it expected, even when that just meant you sent it too fast and a small delay kicked in. Now that situation is quietly noted in the logs instead of sounding the alarm. You won't see a difference on your screen; if anything, it just means fewer false error alerts show up behind the scenes when you wrap up a conversation quickly.

ai.title: Add error details to browser runner startup failure
ai.summary: Startup failure logs now append the raw error message to the standard Chrome installation guidance in `npm-app/src/browser-runner.ts`. This change aids debugging by exposing underlying launch exceptions previously hidden by the generic catch block. Scope limited to internal logging and minor syntax cleanup within the browser runner. Error handling remains non-breaking, preserving existing success/failure return structures.

eli5.text: When the browser tool fails to start, the error message it shows now includes the specific reason it failed, instead of just a generic note about Chrome not being installed. This change affects anyone trying to use the browser-based assistant feature when something goes wrong during startup. If you looked at the error output before and after, you'd see the addition of a line like 'Received error: out of memory' or similar detail that helps pinpoint the cause. This makes troubleshooting faster for the support team and reduces vague bug reports from users.

eli5.text: The version number for the Codebuff tool was updated from 1.0.426 to 1.0.427. This is a routine patch release that packages together several recent improvements made during the past few days. Among other things, the update includes a new model option for advanced reasoning tasks, cleaner organization of internal tool definitions, an additional fallback for handling Claude model requests, and fixes for a few small glitches such as accidental menu triggers when pasting text and issues with canceling terminal commands. It also removes an unused dependency that was previously included. If you updated to this version today, you'd be getting all of those changes combined into one installable update.

ai.title: Terminal shell selection prefers zsh over bash
ai.summary: selectShell in npm-app/src/terminal/run-command.ts now calls detectShell to prefer zsh on non-Windows systems, falling back to bash. buildEnv dynamically sets env.SHELL to /bin/${shell} instead of hardcoding /bin/bash. This aligns the advertised shell with the actual binary started by the terminal agent.

eli5.text: When you open a terminal inside the app, it will now start a zsh shell instead of bash on your computer (macOS or Linux), if zsh is installed. If zsh is not available, it falls back to bash. The terminal process also tells other programs it should use whatever shell it actually started with, so everything stays in sync.

ai.title: Shell support narrowed to bash, zsh, cmd.exe
ai.summary: run-command.ts restricts UnixShell to bash|zsh and WinShell to cmd.exe. Drops fish, ksh, sh, tcsh, nu, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe from type unions and buildInit. Removes PowerShell profile sourcing, fish conf.d loops, and shell-specific shebang/alias branches. Wrapper script generation now hardcodes bash/zsh shebangs and alias expansion flags.

eli5.text: If you run a shell command through the assistant, it now only works with bash, zsh, or Windows' cmd.exe (PowerShell, fish, and other shells are no longer supported). You won't notice this unless you specifically use one of the dropped shells, in which case your commands may fail to start. The change is internal to the assistant software and is live today.
